n: Christ has set us free. So stand firm and don’t let yourselves be harnessed again to a yoke of slavery.

f.w: the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free

n: If they accept circumcision as necessary for salvation, Christ will be of no benefit to them.

f.g: Adopting circumcision as a requirement for salvation.

n: Anyone who accepts circumcision on that basis is obligated to keep the entire law of Moses.

f.w: a debtor to do the whole law

n: Those trying to be justified by the law have cut themselves off from Christ and fallen away from grace.
But through the Spirit, by faith, believers eagerly await the righteousness they hope for.
In Christ, circumcision or lack of it means nothing. What counts is faith that expresses itself through love.
They were running the race well. Who cut in and tripped them up from obeying the truth?

f.g: Literally “cut in on” — like a runner blocked on the track.

n: This persuasion doesn’t come from God, who called them.
A little yeast works through the whole batch of dough — a little false teaching can corrupt the whole community.

f.w: A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump

n: Paul is confident in the Lord they’ll agree with him. Whoever is troubling them will bear God’s judgment.
If Paul still preached circumcision, as some claimed, why is he persecuted? Preaching circumcision would remove the offense of the cross.
With biting sarcasm, Paul wishes those so eager for cutting would cut themselves off completely.

f.g: A sharp play on words about circumcision; possibly “mutilate themselves.”

n: They were called to freedom — but not as an excuse to indulge selfish desires. Instead, serve one another in love.

f.g: An opportunity for the sinful nature.

n: The whole law is summed up in one command: love your neighbor as yourself.

f.w: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself

n: If they bite and devour each other like wild animals, they’ll end up destroying one another.
Live by the Spirit, and you won’t carry out the desires of the sinful nature.

f.g: Desires of the fallen, natural self.

n: The flesh and the Spirit are at war with each other, pulling in opposite directions.

f.w: the flesh lusteth against the Spirit

n: Those led by the Spirit are not under the law’s condemnation.
The works of the sinful nature are obvious: sexual sin, impurity, and shameless sensuality.
Idolatry, sorcery, hostility, conflict, jealousy, rage, rivalry, divisions, and factions.

f.g: Greek pharmakeia — sorcery, often involving drugs.

n: Envy, murder, drunkenness, wild partying, and the like. Paul warns again: those who live this way won’t inherit God’s kingdom.

f.w: shall not inherit the kingdom of God

n: But the fruit the Spirit grows in us is love, joy, peace, patience, gentleness, goodness, and faithfulness. Note it is one “fruit” — a single harvest of Christlike character.
Meekness and self-control. No law forbids such things.
Those who belong to Christ have crucified the sinful nature with its passions and desires.
Since the Spirit gives us life, let us keep in step with the Spirit.

f.g: Keep in step, march in line.

n: Let’s not be conceited, provoking and envying each other.
